Stacking appears only on `.set-row`, `.set-agent-row`, `.mach-row`, `.rail-card` and `.kb-row`, none of which is a dense list. The six inline rules, read off five shipping rows that agree on all six:

1. **The agent mark leads the row**, `flex: 0 0 auto`. It does not follow the name.
2. **The name is `flex: 0 1 auto` with a measured floor, never `flex: 1` and never `min-width: 0`.** `--sm-name-min` is measured with `measureText` on the live element at `--text-base`/`--weight-medium` over real session names, the way `app.css:198-220` records for `.ptab-name`'s 46px; the number and the method go in this entry's proof, and the probe holds it. It is **not** added to `gate:tab-floor`'s table — that gate measures a different surface at a different size — and if the measurement proves unstable the stated fallback is a row in that table rather than a chosen number.
3. **The folder is the field that gives way**, `flex: 0 100 auto; min-width: 0`, an order of magnitude above the name's shrink factor. `search.css:328-333` records the measurement that forced it: equal shrink truncated `shot-hook.ts` while `src/renderer/editor` still had room, "exactly backwards, since the name is the thing being looked for".
4. **A dedicated spacer takes the slack**, `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: var(--space-3)`, never a field.
5. **Trailing marks are `flex: 0 0 auto`**, so the removal date is sized by its own content and right-aligned, with the exact time still on hover.
6. **The folder truncates from the RIGHT.** `.scm-row-dir` truncates left with `direction: rtl`, and `search.css:357-362` refuses exactly that for paths and says why: bidi reordering moves the `/` and `.` runs so a path can render with its separators in the wrong places and land mid-word with no ellipsis at all. `PastList.tsx:123` already carries the whole path as the row's `title`, so the hover half is built.

**The promise cannot be inline, and the sentence is not lost.** "Restore continues the conversation" / "starts fresh" is a sentence, and no row in either tree carries a sentence. The app already solved this: `.srow-saved` is a ↺ mark at `--text-secondary` and `session-rail.css:207-218` says the resume sentence is "a paragraph under the scan line, not part of it" and puts it in the hover card. So the Past row draws the ↺ mark inline at `flex: 0 0 auto` and keeps the sentence in the row's `title` and in the inline panel, which already has it. That removes the widest field from the row and is most of what buys the density.

**Refused, with the reason.** The state does not become a chip: it is the shipped `.dot` plus the shipped label, and a pill around it would be the second status-looking mark `machine-badge.css:9-11` already refuses in these words. The machine is not repeated as text: the badge is the one bearer. And a machine-removed Past row keeps `.sm-past-note` on its own line and is the one row in the sheet above 40px, because its tombstone is a sentence and rule 6 applies to it too.

### The mechanism

Every colour and every space from a token, no literal outside the one geometry block, the hit areas kept, and the DOM contract of SPEC §2.14 untouched — it names element types and `data-*` attributes (`table.sm-grid`, `tr.sm-group`, `tr.sm-row`, `.sm-past-row`, `section.sm-past-group`, `[data-sm="foot"]`, `[data-manage-*]`) and not one CSS value, so `probe:p293` and `conformance:manager` read exactly what they read today. The sheet's geometry already lives as custom properties on ONE selector, `session-manager.css:33-59`; this phase edits that block and three numbers outside it, which is why it is cheap.

1. **The row.** `--sm-row-h: calc(28px + 2 * var(--space-3))` replaces `--sm-past-row: 64px` and `--sm-skeleton-row: 62px`; `tbody td` padding `var(--space-6) var(--space-5)` → `var(--space-3) var(--space-5)`; `tr.sm-row` and `.sm-past-row` state `height`/`min-height: var(--sm-row-h)`. The select cell keeps `padding: 0 0 0 var(--space-4)` (`:343-347`), which is what lets its 32×32 target keep its size.
2. **One name size.** `.sm-grid`'s `font-size: var(--text-sm)` goes; the grid inherits `body`'s `--text-base`/`--lh-base`, and `.sm-name strong` states `--text-base` so the Managed tab and the Past tab draw one size. `--weight-medium` is kept: the app is split between regular (`.srow-name`) and medium (`.ptab`, `.prail-open`, `.set-agent-name`, `.rail-card-name`), and four of five is not a case for changing it.
3. **One secondary field.** `td > small` (`:324-330`) and `.sm-name small` (`:420-425`) become one class at `--text-xs`/`--lh-xs` `--text-secondary`, drawn **inline** at `--space-3`; `line-height: 1.5` goes from both sites (`:328`, `:423`). The two different gaps become one thing that no longer exists.
4. **The heading idiom, the single biggest type divergence.** `thead th` (`:289`) gains all four properties — `--text-xs`/`--lh-xs`, `--weight-medium`, `text-transform: uppercase`, `letter-spacing: var(--track-caps)` — with `padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-5)`, giving 28px. Its colour stays **`--text-secondary` and not the idiom's `--text-muted`**, because the heading's ground is `--bg-raised` where `--text-muted` measures under the floor; that is the one deliberate deviation and `p293-css-tokens.test.ts` already forbids the alternative. **The rule under it stays a `box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0`**, never a border: a border on a sticky `th` under `border-collapse: collapse` drops out in Chromium.
5. **The titles reach the app's step.** `.sm-heading` and `.sm-state-block h2` go from `--text-md` to `--text-lg`/`--lh-lg`, matching `.modal-title` and `.empty-title`; `.sm-state-block p` to `--text-base`/`--lh-base`, matching `.empty-body`; `.sm-tab` to `--text-base`, matching `.ptab` and `.stab`; `.sm-select` to `--text-sm`, which is `--view-field-text`, the step every field in the app reads at minimum. The 52px title bar does not move and a 28px line box clears it with 12px to spare — the comment at `:94` was about the 20px size beside a 15px tab label, not about the bar's height.
6. **The chips reuse the primitive.** `.sm-count`'s `min-width: 19px; padding: 2px 5px` (`:146-147`) and `.sm-chip`'s `padding: 1px 6px` (`:509`) — 19, 5 and 1 are on no grid — become `.chip-sm` (`globals.css:345-349`: `height: 16px; font-size: var(--text-2xs); padding: 0 var(--space-2)`) with `min-width: 16px` from `.ab-badge`. The result is the same 16px box the machine badge beside them already is.
7. **The transitions, which do not exist today.** `transition: background var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out)` on `.sm-grid tbody td` and `.sm-past-row`; background and colour on `.sm-icon-btn`, `.sm-tab` and `.sm-sort`; and `.btn.sm-end`'s hover names `background, border-color, color`, because it moves three properties today and `.btn` animates one. `--dur-fast` is the step `.scm-row` and `.ptab` use, and a modal table row is closest in kind to those. **No `prefers-reduced-motion` block**: `tokens.css:655-697` covers it app-wide, which is the reason to write the durations as tokens.
8. **One icon-button vocabulary.** `.sm-icon-btn` re-implements `.icon-btn` from scratch and inherits none of it, while `.sm-panel-icon` in the same sheet correctly derives. The four call sites (`ManagedGrid.tsx:205`, `SessionManagerSheet.tsx:496, 505, 530`) gain `icon-btn`, the class keeps only placement and its 28px size, and its hover comes to `--bg-raised`, the value twenty `.icon-btn` sites use — except on a row, where the row's own hover already took `--bg-raised`, so the row's button keeps `--bg-active` with that reason written beside it.
9. **The icon sizes.** `AgentIcon size={19}` (`ManagedGrid.tsx:234`) → no `size` at all, taking the component's own 16 default, so the call site cannot drift again. `Codicon size={28}` (`SessionManagerSheet.tsx:156`) → 24, the app's ceiling and one of the four sanctioned exceptions. `debug-stop` (`SessionManagerSheet.tsx:555`) → `close` at `sm`, which is the glyph the app already draws for ending a session and the only one in `MENU_CODICONS`. `unfold` (`ManagedGrid.tsx:344`) → `arrow-both`. `folder` at `md` (`ManagedGrid.tsx:76`) → `lg`, matching `ProjectRail.tsx:260`. The Past tab's `history` is drawn at `md` through the shared tab at `SessionManagerSheet.tsx:194` while the row's is `sm` at `ManagedGrid.tsx:188`; both become `sm`. The two tab marks themselves stay — `icon="terminal"` at `SessionManagerSheet.tsx:481` and `icon="history"` at `:489` — because DESIGN-SPEC S15 names them, with the reason recorded.
10. **The tab underline.** `left: 0; right: 0` with no radius becomes `left/right: var(--space-2)` with `border-radius: var(--r-bar) var(--r-bar) 0 0`, matching `settings.css:572-583`, the app's only other tab underline; `bottom: -1px`, `height: 2px` and `--accent` already agree.
11. **The focus rules, stated rather than implied.** `.sm-select:focus-visible` states all three declarations, as `.set-select` and `.input` do, so a later reader can tell the ring is intended. The four-selector restatement at `panels.css:114-120` is deleted and the global serves. The sheet container's suppressed ring at `:63-67` stays, with its comment strengthened, because the sheet takes focus when a person clicks its empty ground and that is not a control.
12. **The keyboard cursor inside a checked block.** Adopted verbatim from `scm.css:446-456`, which exists for this exact problem: `inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border-strong)` on the row holding the keyboard, `inset 0 0 0 1px var(--accent)` when that row is also checked, both gated on `.sm-scroll:focus-within`. No new token, no new state.
13. **Declared, not changed.** The checked row keeps `border-bottom-color: var(--border-active)` rather than `.srow.selected`'s inset outline, and the reason is written down: a full-width table row on `--bg-surface` is not `.srow` on `--bg-sidebar`, and `project-rail.css:159-166` already forbids copying that outline onto a full-bleed row. The row's action buttons (`ManagedGrid.tsx:329`, `PastList.tsx:140`) stay permanently drawn rather than revealed on hover, and that is written into the file too, because a management sheet's verbs are the reason the sheet exists — it reads as an omission today only because nothing says so.
14. **The breakpoint inverts, and this is a defect the change would otherwise introduce.** `@media (max-width: 1100px)` (`:645-652`) sets `td` to `var(--space-5) var(--space-4)` = 12/8, which is shorter than today's 16/12 and *taller* than the pick's 6/12. It becomes `var(--space-3) var(--space-4)`, changing only the horizontal term, and a unit case over the stylesheet pins that the narrow row is never taller than the wide one. The `@media` keeps its literal 1100 because a custom property is not readable in a media query, and the comment says so.
15. **The skeleton was derived from the old row.** 62 + the `--space-4` gap = 70, which is exactly the old two-line pitch, so against a 40px row the loading state is 30px per row too tall and the list visibly resettles when the real rows land. The skeleton reads `--sm-row-h` and `.sm-loading`'s gap goes to 0, so the pitch is the row's own. It is already 6px wrong on the Past tab today.
16. **The numbers the row's height derives.** `--sm-past-state: 145px` is deleted, because rule 5 makes the date content-sized. `--sm-actions-min: 170px` (`:44`) is re-derived from what it actually holds — a `.btn`, a 28px ellipsis and a `--space-3` gap measure about 106px — and its second job as the Past row's `flex-basis` at `:560-561` gets its own name. `scroll-margin-top: 60px` (`panels.css:36`) becomes `calc(var(--sm-head-h) + var(--space-6))`, which is what 60 always was: the sticky heading's height plus a gap. The batch list's `max-height: 144px` (`panels.css:219`) cuts its fifth 33px row mid-row; it becomes `calc(4 * 33px + var(--space-5))`, four whole rows and a visible hint of the fifth, and `.saved-output-body`'s `96px`/`320px` (`panels.css:186-187`) move into the same block.
17. **Classes for the nodes whose type this phase rewrites.** `td > small`, `.sm-name small`, `.sm-state-block h2` and `.sm-state-block p` are the only bare-element selectors carrying type, and the phase is rewriting exactly those four declarations, so they gain classes the way `.set-row-label` and `.srow-name` have them. The panels' `dt`/`dd` stay.
18. **`conformance:manager`'s read half and `p293-css-tokens.test.ts` grow the rules that hold all of this.** The test file already reads every stylesheet in the domain for colour; it gains: no ratio line-height, every `font-size` paired with a `line-height`, `--text-2xs` nowhere but a chip and the footer, every `padding`/`margin`/`gap` a `--space-*` or a named property on `.modal.session-sheet`, `--track-caps` on any uppercase rule, and — read from the TSX — every `size=` passed to `Codicon` or `AgentIcon` in the domain one of `sm`/`md`/`lg`/16/24. `ablation:p293` gains one ablation per new rule.

**One reversal, so a later round does not "fix" it.** `panels.css:173`, `:181` and `:206` set three `saved-output-*` rules to `--text-secondary` where the modal they were copied from uses `--text-muted`, which looks like a lost subordination. It is not: the inline panel's ground is `--bg-raised`, where `--text-muted` is below the floor, so the flattening is correct and the sheet's own contrast rule requires it. The fix is the missing comment. The five duplicated type declarations beside them are deleted and `saved-output.css` serves.

### The six rough edges Phase 293's verifiers left, fixed in the same phase

1. **Toasts are drawn over the End/Restore column, so a click on a lower row lands on the toast.** `.toasts` is `position: fixed; right: var(--space-6); bottom: var(--space-6)`, 360 wide, `--z-toast` 700 over `--z-modal` 500 (`app.css:2106-2127`, `Toasts.tsx:37`); the scrim leaves the sheet 24px of bottom gutter (`.modal-scrim::after`, `app.css:1455-1458`). One toast overlaps the sheet's bottom 36px, two overlap 88px, three 140px; at 1512 logical px the stack covers the sheet's rightmost 210px, and the actions column is 190px plus its cell padding. So with two toasts up the last row's End button is under the toast, and `SessionManagerSheet.tsx`'s own comment already admits it: "A toast's button still takes its click: the click lands on what is under the pointer." DESIGN-SPEC S15 says nothing is ever stacked on the sheet, and a toast is the one thing that still is. **The fix: while the sheet is open the toast stack docks inside it, above the footer, as a `flex: 0 0 auto` strip, so it takes height from the scroller and covers nothing.** The seam is one outlet ref the toast host portals into. `pointer-events: none` is refused because it would break the pause-on-hover S10 promises; the stated fallback, if the outlet costs more than this phase should spend, is bottom padding on `.sm-scroll` equal to the stack's height, which lets the last row always be scrolled clear.
2. **`0+ / Replies not recorded` beside `No messages yet` on the same row.** Both follow SPEC §3.4 exactly: the Messages table says `partial, agentMessages null → <u>+ / Replies not recorded`, so a gemini record with no kept ask and `userMessages: 0` draws `0+`, while the Last message table's `counts present, total 0` draws `No messages yet` from the same halves. A `+` on a zero promises more where the cell beside it says there is none. **The clause §3.4 lacks:** with `agentMessages` null and `userMessages` 0, `messagesCell` draws the dash and `No messages yet`, the same reading `lastMessageOf` computes from the same halves, and `drawnMessageTotal` answers null so the Messages sort agrees with the cell, which is that function's own stated promise. `copy.ts`, the SPEC table, `p293-copy.test.ts` and `manager-conformance-probe.mts`'s cell fixture move in one commit.
3. **A sort click or a filter change at 300 sessions does not settle inside one frame.** The projection and the view are already memoized (`use-sheet-refresh.ts:110`, `:147`), so the cost is React's render: `ManagedRow` and `PastRow` are not memoized, and a sort re-renders every row — about 33 elements per row read from `ManagedGrid.tsx`, so roughly 10,000 for 300 rows. A sort keeps the row objects *identical* and changes only the array order, so `React.memo` on both row components turns a sort into a reorder in which React moves existing nodes. **The limit, named rather than hidden:** `useNow(10_000)` (`SessionManagerSheet.tsx:209`) is a prop on every row, so the ten-second tick still re-renders all 300; that is a tick and not a press, and closing it is its own entry.
4. **A removed machine is named twice on its row, three times counting the badge.** `tombstoneLine` opens "You removed `<label>` on `<day>`." and `tombstoneRestoreRefused` says "Tortie can no longer reach `<label>`, so it cannot bring this session back." (`settings/machines-copy.ts:463, 489`), and the name line already carries the machine badge. The refusal sentence, in the sheet's own `copy.ts` and not in the shipped `machines-copy.ts` that Settings reads, drops to "Add the machine again to bring this session back." — shorter, still beside the button as Phase 293's ruling requires, and naming no machine.
5. **An ended row with nothing saved draws no line at all**, so the only thing that says why Restore is off is the disabled button's hover title, and the resting face is silent where every other ended row says `Conversation saved` or `Output saved`. `endedSmall`'s null is honest — `Output saved` would be false — but silence is not the only honest answer. The slot draws `Nothing saved`, a label rather than a sentence, with `NOTHING_TO_RESTORE_TITLE` still the hover.
6. **A remote shell reads `— / Shell` where §3.4's table says `— / Unavailable` — and the finding's direction is the opposite of how it looks.** The table is keyed on the activity, and `remoteActivity()` answers `coverage: 'unavailable', reason: 'remote'`, so by the table the cell is `Unavailable`; `messagesCell` short-circuits on `agent === 'shell'` first, so it reads `Shell`. The prose directly under the same table blesses the code: "**In the renderer a shell is decided before remote**, so a shell on another machine reads `— / Shell` … a shell has no messages on any machine, which is the truer word (the matrix verifier's P4)." So the product is right and the spec's own table disagrees with its own prose. The fix is to the table, plus a driven case in `manager-conformance-probe.mts` so a later round cannot silently flip it. **No word a person reads changes.**

### The proof, run rather than read

**A photograph is forbidden in this repository and `npm run shot` may never run**, so every claim above is proved by rectangles and computed styles read in the running app.

- **`probe:p293`, arm 11 widened.** One Electron through `build/electron-run.mjs`, a scratch profile, a scratch `HOME` and its own tmux socket, every session a shell, nothing spawned and no token spent. `P293_ARMS=11` runs it alone; `P293_PARENT_CHECKOUT` points the same run at `f6c11f57` for the parent reading, which is mandatory because the operator reported this. Arm 11's existing readings are the **control and must not move**: both toolbar modes at 47px and the title bar at 52px.
- **Geometry, box and pitch read separately** so the two layout models cannot be conflated. `getBoundingClientRect().height` on `tr.sm-row`, `.sm-past-row`, `.sm-skeleton`, `thead th`, `tr.sm-group > th` and `[data-sm="foot"]`: **40, 40, 40, 28, 28 and 29** at HEAD against **73, 64, 62, 44, 40 and 45** at the parent. The pitch is read as the distance between consecutive row tops: **41** on Managed and **40** on Past at HEAD, against **74** and **64** at the parent.
- **Hit areas, every one at or above its parent reading.** `[data-manage-check]`'s label 32×32, `[data-manage-primary]` 28 tall, the ellipsis 28×28, the title bar's two 28×28. A reading below the parent's fails the arm.
- **Rows per sheet, measured not computed.** The window is sized so the sheet resolves to 900px of height, and the arm counts the `tr.sm-row` rectangles wholly inside the scroller's rect: 9 at the parent, 17 at HEAD on Managed; 11 and 19 on Past.
- **`--sm-name-min` is measured, not chosen.** `measureText` on the live `.sm-name strong` at `--text-base`/`--weight-medium` over the run's own session names plus the longest real names the Phase 137 corpus holds; the number goes into the CSS and into this entry's mechanism, and the arm re-reads it.
- **Nothing is clipped that must not be.** Exactly three elements may ellipsis — the session name, the group header's path, and the Past row's folder — each carrying its whole value as a hover `title`. Every other text node in the sheet is `nowrap` with no `max-width`, so a long honesty word widens the table and `.sm-scroll` scrolls sideways. The arm asserts `scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 1` on every text node but those three, over the longest strings the sheet can say: `Replies not recorded`, `Partial history`, `Session updated`, `Conversation saved`, `Nothing saved`, `Not applicable`, `Unreachable`, and a 60-character folder — at 1180px, at the 1100px breakpoint, and at `calc(100vw - 48px)` on a 1024-wide window. **This is the attack, and it is what protects the honesty words the type change touches.**
- **Computed hover, active, selected, focus and transition.** `getComputedStyle` on a row at rest, under a real pointer, checked, and with its panel open: `backgroundColor` equal to `--bg-raised` and `--bg-active`'s resolved values, `borderBottomColor` equal to `--border-active`'s, and `transitionProperty`/`transitionDuration`/`transitionTimingFunction` equal to `background`/`120ms`/`cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` — zero and `all 0s` at the parent, which is the finding. `boxShadow` on a focused row control equal to `--focus-ring`'s resolved value, read on the FIRST and LAST data row so the sticky heading's fill and the scroller's block-start overflow are both exercised. With `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia` forcing `prefers-reduced-motion`, every duration reads 1ms, which is the proof the durations are tokens and not literals.
- **Icon sizes.** The computed `fontSize` of every `.codicon` in the sheet and the computed `width`/`height` of every `AgentIcon` wrapper: every value in {12, 14, 16, 24} and no 19 and no 28. A single reading outside the set fails the arm.
- **Contrast, through the app's own helper.** Every text node's computed `color` against the computed `backgroundColor` of its nearest painted ancestor, run through `contrastOf` (`src/renderer/theme/hue.ts:87`), at rest and under the pointer and checked, on **both bases** — one Electron reaches both, because the theme flips by the `data-scheme` attribute on `<html>` and there is no `prefers-color-scheme` query anywhere in the tree. Every body text at or above 4.5; a disabled control's label is exempt and named. This is where a `--text-muted` on a raised ground would surface, and it is why the column heading keeps `--text-secondary`.
- **The no-regression side-by-side, under the operator's standing rule.** The same arm at `f6c11f57` and at this HEAD over the same fixture: every row's drawn strings byte-identical, every hit area equal or larger, every contrast equal or higher, the row shorter. A scenario that reads worse at HEAD drops the clause that caused it.
- **Gates.** `typecheck`, `build`, `test`, `smoke:t1`, `conformance:manager` (its cell fixtures move with nit 2 and nit 6), `ablation:p293` with one ablation per new rule, and `probe:p293`. **`conformance:hue` is out of the proof**, about thirteen minutes saved, because no token's value moves and no new text-on-ground pairing is introduced; if a builder adds a token or reaches for `--text-muted` on `--bg-raised` or `--bg-active`, it runs and the pairing is refused. `gate:contract` is untouched — no channel. `HELPER_USER_FLOOR` does not move — no new script reaches `build/electron-run.mjs`. **`docs/DESIGN-SPEC.md` S15's geometry table and `build/p293/SPEC.md` §2.2 and §3.4 move in the same commit**, because S15 is the design authority for this surface and a table that still says 64 and 145 and 28 is a table a later round will build back.

### What is NOT in this phase

- **No new column and no new data.** The seven columns stay, the activity aggregate is untouched, and no channel is added, changed or read differently.
- **No change to what any verb does.** End, Remove, Restore, the batch loop, every gate in `sessionMenuItems()` and every re-check at the press are the same code; `conformance:manager`'s driven half must read exactly what it reads today.
- **No change to the Past order the operator ruled on.** One list in main's order, newest removal first, grouped under a project's heading only when the project filter names one project.
- **No change to any sentence a person reads**, with three named exceptions, each carrying its reason above: the machine's name dropped from the refusal on a tombstoned row, `Nothing saved` in a slot that was empty, and `No messages yet` where `0+` contradicted the cell beside it. The state words, the confirmations and the batch report are byte-identical.
- **No new token.** `tokens.css` is not edited, so nothing needs re-solving on the light base and no contrast floor moves.
- **No hit area below the accessibility floor, and none smaller than today EXCEPT where the row's own height bounds it, each such case named with its arithmetic.** The body row's 32×32 check target, the 28×28 icon buttons, the 24px primary button and the 2px focus ring all keep their sizes, and the arm fails on any reading below the parent's. **THIS REFUSAL IS AMENDED FROM "no hit area smaller than today", which was unsatisfiable as written, and the operator ruled on the amendment himself on 2026-09-20 when the arm measured it.** A control whose height comes from the row cannot keep its absolute pixels in a phase whose entire deliverable is a row 33px shorter, so the original wording could only have been met by giving back the density it was written to protect. Two targets are therefore admitted exceptions, both carried in `probe-p293.mjs`'s `HIT_EXCEPTIONS` with their arithmetic, both graded like any other floor so a later round that shrinks either still goes red, and both asked of WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8's 24×24 independently: the **column heading's select-all**, 32×32 to 32×28, which is every reachable pixel of its own 28px row and could otherwise only take pixels from the toolbar above or, under its cell's `z-index`, from the first data row's own checkbox; and the **row's name button**, 37 tall to 28, which is the whole of its cell's content box where the parent's was 51 percent of a 73px one. The alternatives were measured and refused in front of him: holding the name button at 37 forces the row to about 49 and costs three of the seventeen rows, and making the whole `tr` clickable is a behaviour change rather than a density fix and needs its own phase. The 24×24 floor is now its own clause in the arm, independent of the parent, because "no smaller than today" never protected a control that was already too small. **A THIRD case was admitted the same evening and it is a different kind, so the words above cover height and this one covers width**: the **Managed tab** is 101.2px wide against the parent's 102.3, 1.1px narrower with its height unmoved, because mechanism 6 did what this entry asked and replaced an ad-hoc `span.sm-count` at 19×17 with the app's own `span.chip-sm.sm-count` at 16×16 — 19, 5 and 1 sit on no grid. The Past tab got WIDER by the same change, 129.08 to 129.76, which is the clearest evidence this is the chip's size rather than a shrinking tab, and 101×51 is nowhere near the 24×24 floor. He refused both alternatives: a `min-width` on the sheet's tabs, and keeping a chip size that exists nowhere else in Tortie. **AND THE WAY IT WAS FOUND IS THE REASON THIS REFUSAL IS WORTH ANYTHING NOW.** The app run's own PASS was obtained with **eight of the thirteen enumerated targets carrying no parent floor at all** — the arm printed that in its notes, "NO PARENT READING EXISTS for 8 enumerated target(s), so 'no hit area smaller than today' is NOT asserted about them" — and the reverifier ran the arm the way the fix round's own `P293_HIT_PARENT` mechanism intends, feeding a parent run's readings back so the promise is asserted about all thirteen. The same promise read PASS over 7 controls and FAIL over 13. That is this phase's second lesson of the same shape as its first, and the reverifier proved the refusal can now fail by breaking the shipping build five ways, each of which the arm named, including both height exceptions graded below their admitted numbers and the WCAG clause firing on its own.
- **The 52px title bar and the 47px toolbar do not move.** By the phase's own formula the token answer for both is 44, and that is a real counter-example a reviewer will find — it is named here and refused, because they are the operator's own geometry from the design study, `probe:p293` arm 11 pins them, and moving them would put a 6px change to the sheet's frame inside a phase about its rows. Their own entry if he wants it.
- **No hover-revealed row actions**, no fifth selected-row treatment, no row radius, and no `:active` state: the sheet's fill-only selection and permanent verbs are declared in the file rather than changed.
- **No release.**


## Phase 299 — the counts a row draws (Phase 293's counts verifier, 2026-09-19)

**Subject.** `fix(overview): the counts a row draws are that session's own`

**First body line.** `Phase 299: three counting defects the session manager inherited`

**Semver.** Patch. Three things change on the Manage Sessions sheet and in Catch Me Up, and nothing else on either surface moves. A codex session whose reply was written only as an `AgentMessage`, on a turn that closed with no `last_agent_message`, counts that reply instead of losing it. A row whose conversation id names a record belonging to a different folder stops drawing that folder's numbers as `complete` and draws a dash with `Not recorded`, which is the word the sheet already has for a record it cannot honestly count. And a slash command typed with no arguments counts as the person's message, so the reply to it stops replacing the previous turn's reply and a session driven only by one stops reading `No messages yet`. No verb, no column, no channel and no sentence a person reads changes.

**Tier 3.** By CLAUDE.md's second question: the keep map is the one piece of data every provider is read through, and this phase edits two providers' rules and the engine that reads them, so the claim is a claim across agents and providers and **the evidence is a per-row matrix over real data**. Two independent methods, one of them an attack. The first is **re-derive independently**: a verifier writes its own counter over the real store by a third method — neither the overview store's SQL nor the Phase 293 verifier's own log walk — and compares per session at the parent and at HEAD. The second is **a hostile fixture**, because every one of these three defects is a rule about bytes somebody else wrote: a part type spelled four ways, a recorded folder that is absent, one that differs only by case, one that differs only by NFC against NFD, a bare command that is on the drop list, a bare command as the only message and a bare command mid-session. **The parent-commit measurement is mandatory whatever the tier**, because every number below is a claim about the parent and the table in CLAUDE.md says that measurement is the only honest proof a defect is fixed. It is not Tier 3 for the other reasons: nothing here can lose the person's work (the reader opens agent logs read only and writes only Tortie's own overview store), nothing spawns, nothing holds a credential and nothing sends the person's words anywhere.

**Charter.** Phase 293's Tier 3 **counts verifier**, 2026-09-19, which wrote its own counter from the provider logs by a different method than the store's SQL and compared the two per session. It returned three findings, C1 to C3. All three are minor, all three are inherited from the Phase 137 reader or from harvest rather than caused by Phase 293, and all three were **recorded as stated limits when 293 landed** at `f6c11f57`: `build/p293/SPEC.md:83-88` states them in §1's limits, `:2132-2141` states them again in the verification findings with the remedy each one wants, `:2259` routes them to §9, and the running log's landing line names all three as "STILL NOT TRUE and each queued next as its own entry". This is that entry for the three of them. C4, C5, the Refresh that re-opens a closed remote project tab and the lost tombstone are the other entries the same line queued and are not in this one.

### What was measured before this entry was written, so no round re-derives it

The verifier's readings are quoted. Everything else was measured for this entry, read only, on 2026-09-19: the real stores with `rg` and `find`, and the tree at origin/main's tip in `/private/tmp/wt-release`, which carries no `node_modules`, so every source reading is read and not executed.

**The verifier's three findings, in its numbers.**

- **C1.** Every one of the **4,767** `AgentMessage` parts it counted on this Mac, across codex **0.149.1 through 0.154.0**, carries `type: "Text"`. The keep map's `partWhen` asks for `"text"`, which is the spelling in the committed fixture. A turn whose `task_complete` carries no `last_agent_message` therefore loses its reply and the row under-counts.
- **C2.** **Five of 110** resolved local claude and codex rows are bound by the weak harvest keys `cwd-newest` and `boot-rescue`, and their conversation id names a record whose own cwd is a **different folder**, so the sheet draws that other folder's counts for this session and draws them as `complete`.
- **C3.** An argument-less slash command is not counted as the person's message. Its example row reads **`— / No messages yet`**.

**The codex store, measured here.** 26,312 `rollout-*.jsonl` records under `~/.codex/sessions`, 12 GB. Every count in this block is a line count over every one of those files — the whole store, 2024 through 2026 — except the `cli_version` reading, which names its own window.

- **94,841** `event_msg` records carrying an `item_completed` `AgentMessage`, and the first content part is spelled **`Text` on all 94,841**. A search of the whole store for an `AgentMessage` whose content holds a part spelled `text`, in any position, returns **0**. So the branch the map actually wants matches nothing on this machine, and the figure is twenty times the verifier's because this is the whole store rather than the rows the sheet drew.
- **0** `event_msg` records of type `agent_message` anywhere in the store. The codex answer slot's first `firstOf` branch, `payload.message`, fires on nothing, so the `AgentMessage` branch is the only one that can read a reply out of a record.
- **34,805** `task_complete` records **across the whole store, not a sampled window**, and **2,890 of those 34,805** carry `last_agent_message` as `""` or `null`, which is **8.3 percent**. Those 2,890 are exactly the turns the `answerFrom` rescue cannot supply, and they are the turns that lose their reply today. The complementary count of non-empty ones reads 31,916 rather than 31,915 because one line matches both patterns — a reply that quotes a `task_complete` record — so **2,890 of 34,805 is the pair a later round re-measures against**, and the one-line overlap is why the two halves sum to 34,806.
- `payload.cli_version` **over 2026/09 only** reads 0.152.0, 0.152.1, 0.153.0, 0.153.4, 0.154.0 and **0.155.1** — one release above the verifier's stated ceiling, and `Text` on every one of them.
- The item kinds inside `event_msg`/`item_completed`, over a bounded scan window that undercounts the long ones: Reasoning 23,529, AgentMessage 21,532, UserMessage 2,538, SubAgentActivity 184, ContextCompaction 105. The exact `AgentMessage` figure is the 94,841 above; the ordering is what the scan is for, and the map correctly reads none of the other four.

**The claude store, measured here.** 21,154 `*.jsonl` records under **2,776** project directories in `~/.claude/projects`, 12 GB.

- **2,835** records carry a `<command-name>`. **650** of those carry `<command-args></command-args>`, an empty argument span.
- Those 650 records carry **659** command names, nine more names than records because a few replies quote a command block. **444 of the 659** name one of the nine entries in the map's own `dropCommands` and are meant to be dropped, and the remaining **215 of the 659, across 28 distinct names, are commands the map intends to KEEP** and which `commandEcho` empties instead — 444 + 215 = 659, over 650 records: `/compact` 46, `/workflows` 44, `/fast` 21, `/exit` 17, `/context` 12, `/low-priority` 10, `/doctor` 10, `/usage` 9, `/rate-limit-options` 6, `/voice` 5, `/plugin` 5, `/security-review` 4, `/reload-plugins` 3, `/help` 3, `/btw` 3 and a tail. **215 of the 650 empty-argument records is C3's size on this Mac.**

**Why a green gate said nothing for 162 phases, and this is the most important reading here.** `docs/research/assets/63-fixtures/codex-rollout-2026-08-19T10-05-03-0000aaaa-1111-7000-8000-222233334444.jsonl:13` spells the part **`text`**, lowercase, so on the fixture the `AgentMessage` branch matches. And all three of the fixture's `task_complete` records (`:14`, `:17`, `:22`) carry a **non-empty** `last_agent_message`, so `answerFrom` supplies every answer and the branch is never needed. `conformance:overview`'s pinned `codex answers: 3` (`build/conformance-overview.mjs:159-176`) is therefore **invariant under the defect**: break the branch and the count does not move. The gate cannot see this without a fixture record that spells the part the way every real record spells it *and* closes its turn with an empty `last_agent_message`.

**The source, read at origin/main's tip.**

- **The codex answer slot.** `src/main/overview/keep-map.json:585-600`: `firstOf` is `{ "field": "payload.message" }` then `{ "parts": "payload.item.content", "partWhen": { "eq": ["type", "text"] }, "take": "text", "join": "\n" }`. The turn's rescue is `:626-630`, `answerFrom: { "field": "payload.last_agent_message" }` on `task_complete`, with `pick: "close-answer-else-last-answer"`.
- **The version and what it forces.** `keep-map.json:2` `"mapVersion": 1` and a `"version": 1` per provider at `:13` (claude) and `:352` (codex); the file's own note says "Each provider carries a version. Bump it when the provider's rules change, so stored watermarks retire and the next read is full." `reader/map.ts:23-27` `providerVersion` reads it. `service.ts:279-286` reuses a stored watermark **only** when `prior.mapVersionAtLastRead === mapVersion` and the path is unchanged, so a bump hands `null` and the next read is full from byte 0. `store.ts:360-364` and `:13-21`: `replaceTurnsFrom` deletes the tail, inserts and stamps the watermark, the map version and the read time in **one durable transaction**, so a full re-read replaces every stored turn and a crash inside it leaves the previous state readable. There is no migration, no new deletion path and nothing to back-fill.
- **The state C2 needs already exists.** `reader/resolve.ts:54` declares `{ state: 'wrong-conversation'; provider; file; detail }`. Its only two call sites today are `:125` and `:182-183`, **both antigravity**. `service.ts:255-271` carries it forward and stores it; `overview/activity-map.ts:156` maps the read state to the reason; `src/shared/overview.ts:210` already reads `'wrong-conversation' // the record names a different folder`; `renderer/overview/copy.ts:76-77` is the page's sentence and `renderer/session-manager/__tests__/p293-copy.test.ts:511-524` pins the sheet's cell for it as **`— / Not recorded`**. C2 adds no copy, no channel, no contract line and no token.
- **Both doors C2 comes through.** `resolve.ts:134-143`, claude: the direct path is `<projects>/dashEncodeClaudeCwd(realCwd)/<id>.jsonl`, and **on a miss the loop at `:138-141` accepts `<id>.jsonl` under any of the 2,776 directories** and answers `resolved`. `resolve.ts:144-167`, codex: the day shards are scanned newest-first by the `-<id>.jsonl` suffix and the record's own folder is never asked. The fallback is not itself wrong — a session can `cd`, and a project opened through a symlink resolves elsewhere — which is why the fix must ask the record's own field rather than the directory's name.
- **The comparison costs no extra I/O, because the value is already in the result.** `reader/containers.ts:192-195` reads the record's own folder out of the log during the pass it already makes (`join.cwdField`, `cwd` for claude, `payload.cwd` off `session_meta` for codex), `:356-364` hands it back as `ContainerJoin.cwd` (`:46-50`), and `reader/index.ts:52` carries it on `ReadResult.join.cwd`. **`service.ts` never reads it.** A grep for `result.join` in `src/main/overview` returns nothing.
- **The data has said since Phase 137 what the code does not do.** `keep-map.json:22` declares `"confirm": "cwd"` on claude's join. `reader/map-types.ts:186-193` `JoinCfg` declares `resolve`, `cwdField`, `sessionIdField`, `metaRecord`, `reject` and an index signature; `confirm` falls into the index signature and **nothing anywhere reads it**.
- **Why the two keys are weak.** `harvest/claim-strength.ts:55-61`: `IDENTITY_HARVEST_KEYS` is `tmux-pane`, `pid`, `fd-owner` only, and everything else "keys on the DIRECTORY or on nothing, and a directory is not an identity", so `claimStrengthForKey` rates `cwd-newest` at `matched` and never `confirmed`. `harvest/stores.ts:528-529` is codex's `cwd-newest` (deepseek `:762`, pi `:853`, omp `:942`, opencode `:1080` share it). `manifest/agents.ts:665-679`: `boot-rescue` is the provenance **source** when the watcher started at a later launch rather than with the pane, "so a cwd keyed store is being separated by time alone".
- **One place this entry differs from the verifier's account, and it matters for where the fix goes.** claude has **no entry in `DESCRIPTORS`** (`harvest/stores.ts:508`) at all — it pre-assigns its id with `--session-id` (`agents/registry.ts:532`), so a claude row's id is its own and no harvest key binds it. The claude half of C2 therefore does **not** come from harvest. It comes from `resolve.ts:138-141`. The codex half comes from both: a `matched` claim on a directory, and a shard scan that never asks the record's folder. The fix is in the reader for both, which is why one change closes both halves.
- **C3, the rule that is in code.** `reader/expr.ts:204-213`, `commandEcho`: `t = (op.dropCommands ?? []).includes(name.trim()) || args.trim() === '' ? '' : (name.trim() + ' ' + args.trim()).trim()`. The **`args.trim() === ''`** clause is the whole of C3 and it is in the engine. Its only configuration is `keep-map.json:80-95`, which names `nameTag`, `argsTag` and `dropCommands` and cannot express it. The emptied text then hits `keep-map.json:224-229`, the `empty after transform` drop rule, and the ask is dropped.
- **The turn-folding C3 causes, and it has two shapes.** `keep-map.json:281-288`: claude's turn is `open: "ask"`, `close: "nextAskOr"`, `pick: "last-answer-before-close"`. `reader/fold.ts:219-228`: a **kept** ask flushes the open turn and opens a new one; a dropped ask does not, it falls through to `:229`. `fold.ts:232-235`: an answer is kept only `if (answer?.kind === 'kept' && this.cur)`. So a bare command **as a session's first message** leaves `this.cur` null and **the reply is discarded outright** — the record reads zero turns, which is the verifier's `— / No messages yet`. A bare command **mid-session** leaves the previous turn open, appends the reply there, and `last-answer-before-close` makes it the reply that turn draws: the turn count is one low **and** the previous turn's drawn reply is the reply to a message nobody can see.
- **The comparator, and the trap inside it.** `src/main/fs/folder-identity.ts:186-222` `sameFolder`: byte-equal strings are `'same'` with no syscall, matching `dev`+`ino` is `'same'`, **a proven-absent side is `'different'`**, and anything else is `'unknown'`, never `'different'`. Its doc at `:199-201` records that no Phase 274 caller acts on `'unknown'` and that every caller takes the `'different'` branch for it.
- **One more trap for whoever edits a predicate.** `reader/expr.ts:52-57`: `test` reads `Object.keys(pred)[0]` and **ignores every other key**. A predicate written with two keys silently tests only the first. There is no `in` op (`:59-113` is the whole vocabulary), so any "accept either spelling" must be written with `or`.
- **What a re-read costs.** `overview/activity.ts:30-33` reads rows one at a time and **yields to the event loop between rows**, not inside one, and `:36-40` serialises calls on one module-level chain. `service.ts:288-296` is the one read path and it is the same one `overview:activity` uses. `build/p293/SPEC.md:89-92` measures a first read at **up to about 0.8 s for a 196 MB codex record** with the page cache warm, which is C4 and is not fixed here. A codex bump re-reads every codex row once and a claude bump re-reads every claude row once, each at the next ask, each paying that once. `store.ts:25-28` measures the store's growth at **0.166 percent** of log bytes, so a full re-read stores no more than it stores today.

### The mechanism

Three items. C2 the store can answer with no re-read of history; **C1 and C3 each need one, and in both cases the re-read is forced by a keep-map version bump rather than arranged by hand.**

1. **C1 — the codex answer slot accepts both spellings, and codex's version goes to 2.** `keep-map.json:592-597`'s `partWhen` becomes `{ "or": [ { "eq": ["type", "Text"] }, { "eq": ["type", "text"] } ] }`. `or` and `eq` both already exist (`expr.ts:62-69`), so no engine change and no new op — and the `or` form is required rather than preferred, because `test` reads only the first key of a predicate object. Then `keep-map.json:352` `"version": 1` becomes `2`, which is what makes the fix reach records already read: every codex session's stored watermark stops matching at `service.ts:282`, the next read is full from byte 0, and `replaceTurnsFrom` replaces every stored turn in one transaction. The rescue at `:626-630` stays exactly as it is and keeps winning where it has text, because `pick` is `close-answer-else-last-answer`; what changes is the 8.3 percent of turns where it has none. **This is the one item where a row's count goes up**, and it goes up only on those turns.

2. **C2 — the record's own folder decides, and the answer is `wrong-conversation`.** The reader already carries the record's folder on `ReadResult.join.cwd`; `service.ts` compares it to `row.cwd` with `sameFolder` from `src/main/fs/folder-identity.ts` and, on a refusal, takes the branch `:255-271` already has. Four clauses, each one a line a later round can delete:
   - **`'different'` alone is not enough.** `sameFolder` answers `'different'` when either side is *proven absent*, so a session whose project folder has been deleted, or a record naming a folder that has gone, would have a good record refused. The refusal requires `'different'` **and** both folders to stat, and an absent or unreadable side leaves the row `resolved` exactly as it is today. This is the **first caller in the tree to treat `'unknown'` differently from `'different'`**, so `folder-identity.ts:199-201`'s note moves in the same commit rather than being left saying something untrue.
   - **Identity, never spelling.** Phase 274's rule 23 binds: the comparison is `dev`+`ino`, never a case fold and never a `.normalize()`. `RealName` against `realname` on a case-separating volume is two real folders and must read `different`; the same path in NFC against NFD must read `same`. `conformance:samefolder` already drives both rows on both kinds of volume and this phase adds no new comparison of its own.
   - **The claude directory name is never the evidence.** The fallback at `resolve.ts:138-141` stays, because a session can `cd` and a project can be opened through a symlink. What decides is the record's `cwd` field, which `containers.ts:192-195` already reads.
   - **Nothing is deleted.** The store keeps the turns it read from the other folder and the truth table refuses to draw them: `activity-map.ts:148-157` maps the read state to reason `wrong-conversation` with coverage `unavailable`, and invariant 1 in `src/shared/overview.ts:229-233` makes every value field null. No schema change, no new deletion path and no migration.

   **The exchange this makes, stated plainly because the no-regression rule will be asked about it.** Those five rows lose a number and gain `— / Not recorded`. A count that is another folder's conversation is not this row's count, so replacing it with the word the sheet already has for "I cannot honestly count this" is not a row's count getting worse. Every other row is bound by the rule as written, and the matrix must show that no row counting correctly today counts differently tomorrow except upward under C1 and C3.

3. **C3 — the bare-command rule moves out of the engine and into the map, and claude's version goes to 2.** The `commandEcho` op gains one field, so the decision lives where the keep map's own note says a vendor rule lives ("A vendor change edits this file, not the code"), and `expr.ts:209`'s second clause becomes conditional on it. Claude's `keep-map.json:80-95` sets it so a bare command reads as its own name: `/as-built-architecture` is counted as the person's message and the reply to it opens its own turn. **The `dropCommands` list keeps its job unchanged** — the `||` at `:209` checks the list first, so a bare `/model`, `/status`, `/login` or `/effort` is still dropped, which is 444 of the 650 records measured above and is the behaviour that must not move. Then `keep-map.json:13` `"version": 1` becomes `2` and every claude row is re-read once. Two things stop being wrong at once: the 215 records whose command was emptied are counted, and the previous turn stops drawing the reply to an invisible message as its own.

**The one question in this phase that is the operator's, and this entry does not answer it.** `build/p293/SPEC.md:2140-2141` already records it as copy he rules on: **should a session that holds only an argument-less command read `No messages yet`?** The fix above removes his *example* — that row now counts one ask and one reply — but it does not remove his *question*, because a record can still hold agent text and no kept ask by other routes, among them codex's own goal loop and `dropTurnsWithNoAsk` at `keep-map.json:634-636`. `NO_MESSAGES_WORD` at `src/renderer/session-manager/copy.ts:240` is left byte-for-byte as it is, and the alternative reading — that a record holding agent text but no kept ask should say something other than "no messages" — waits for him. It is his ruling and no builder in this phase makes it. C6's `0+` beside it, recorded on the same line of the SPEC, is not in this phase either.

### The proof, run rather than read

**A photograph is forbidden in this repository and `npm run shot` may never run.** Every number below is read out of a gate, a probe or the real store.

- **`conformance:overview`'s per-provider matrix, with the codex row gaining the fixture that can fail.** A new record is appended to `docs/research/assets/63-fixtures/codex-rollout-2026-08-19T10-05-03-0000aaaa-1111-7000-8000-222233334444.jsonl` — or a sibling 0.154-shaped fixture is added beside it, whichever keeps the banked ratio honest — holding an `item_completed` `AgentMessage` whose part type is **`Text`** on a turn whose `task_complete` carries `last_agent_message: ""`. The codex row's pinned `answers` moves by exactly that record and the `ratio/banked` tolerance of 0.05 is re-derived rather than widened. **`answers: 3` invariant under the defect is the reading this fixture exists to end**, and the gate must print the codex row red at the parent with the new fixture in place.
- **A red-before reading per finding, taken at the parent commit.** Three separate readings, each one the gate or the suite refusing at `f6c11f57` and passing at HEAD, so no fix rides on another's evidence: the codex fixture above; a claude fixture whose only message is `<command-name>/as-built-architecture</command-name>` with an empty `<command-args>`, which must read one ask and one reply at HEAD and zero turns at the parent, plus a second where the bare command sits between two real turns, which must leave the previous turn's reply as its own; and a resolver fixture placing `<id>.jsonl` under a project directory whose record names another folder, which must read `wrong-conversation` at HEAD and `resolved` with the other folder's turns at the parent. Each of the three is also driven with its rule ablated one at a time, so the gate is proved able to go red on the clause that owns it.
- **The hostile fixture set, and this is the attack.** Written by the verifier, not the builder. Part type `Text`, `text`, `TEXT` and `Texts` — the first two kept, the last two not. A record whose recorded folder is **absent** (must stay `resolved`, never `wrong-conversation`). Folders differing only by **case** and only by **NFC against NFD**, on both kinds of volume, against `conformance:samefolder`'s §8 table. A record whose folder is a **symlink** to the session's. A bare command that **is** on `dropCommands` (still dropped). A bare command whose name is not a command at all. A codex turn carrying `Text` **and** a non-empty `last_agent_message` (the rescue must still win, and the reply must not be counted twice). A `task_complete` whose `last_agent_message` is whitespace. And a record whose own reply text quotes a `task_complete` line, which is real: two of the counts above disagree by one line for exactly that reason.
- **The per-row matrix over real data, which is the tier's required evidence.** One row per resolved local session across every provider present on this Mac, at `f6c11f57` and at this HEAD, each row carrying agent, provider, harvest key, provenance source, the record's folder, the session's folder, the `sameFolder` answer, the read state, the ask count, the reply count and the drawn cell. The matrix names, per finding, **how many rows move and in which direction**: upward under C1 and C3, and exactly the five C2 rows from a number to a dash. A row that moves for no named reason fails the arm.
- **Re-derivation by a third method.** The verifier's own counter, written without reading this phase's code and without reusing Phase 293's verifier, over the same sessions: for codex, every `item_completed` `AgentMessage` and every `task_complete` reconciled against the store's `userMessages`/`agentMessages`; for claude, every `<command-name>` record classified into dropped, kept and bare, reconciled against the turn count. A disagreement means one of the two is wrong and the phase finds out which, the way the Phase 123 verifier did with its own cycle detector.
- **The Phase 137 corpus, read READ ONLY.** `conformance:overview --real <file> --provider <p> --repo <dir>` over real records from both stores — 26,312 codex records and 12 GB, 21,154 claude records under 2,776 directories and 12 GB — and nothing under the person's home is opened for writing, nothing is moved and no record is copied out. The corpus is what proves universality, and the numbers in the block above are the corpus reading the builder starts from rather than re-derives.
- **`conformance:manager`, and only if a cell's word changes.** No cell word changes in this phase: `wrong-conversation` already maps to `— / Not recorded` and `p293-copy.test.ts:511-524` already pins it, and `NO_MESSAGES_WORD` is untouched. The gate runs anyway because `overview:activity`'s answer for five rows changes, and its driven half must read exactly what it reads today. **If a builder finds a word that has to move, that word goes to the operator first**, because the copy in this domain is his ruling.
- **`build/overview-conformance-probe.mts:1021`'s literal 1 becomes `providerVersion(agent)` in the same commit.** A stub that hard-codes the map version is a line that turns into a silent lie the moment a version becomes 2, and the whole point of the bump is that a version is read and not assumed.
- **The no-regression side-by-side, under the operator's standing rule.** The same matrix run at `f6c11f57` and at this HEAD over the same real sessions and the same fixtures: **no row's count may get worse.** Every row that counts correctly today counts identically tomorrow; the rows that move, move upward or move to a named refusal, and each is listed with its reason. A scenario that reads worse at HEAD drops the clause that caused it, including the whole of C2 if the five rows cannot be refused without refusing a sixth that is right.
- **Gates.** `typecheck`, `build`, `test`, `smoke:t1`, `conformance:overview` (the path-triggered gate for `src/main/overview/**`), `conformance:manager`, `conformance:samefolder` (`folder-identity.ts` is read by a new caller), and `ablation:p293` unchanged at 60 of 60. **`gate:contract` is untouched**: no channel, no manifest field, no `gmux.*` key, no `GMUX_*` name and no harness mode, so `docs/audits/contract-baseline.txt` stays at 235 lines. **`HELPER_USER_FLOOR` does not move** at 145 — no new script reaches `build/electron-run.mjs`, because none of this needs an Electron. `build/p293/SPEC.md:83-88` and `:2132-2141` move in the same commit, since a SPEC that still states these three as standing limits is a SPEC a later round will build back.

### What is NOT in this phase

- **C4 and C5 are not in it.** The 0.8 s first read of a large record and the `~/.claude/projects` scan on every ask for a claude row with no record are the next two entries the same running-log line queued. Nothing here makes either worse: no read is added, the yield between rows is untouched, and the version bumps pay their full read once at the next ask rather than on a timer.
- **No worker and no slicing.** The read stays synchronous and stays on main, one row at a time, yielding between rows and not inside one. That is C4's fix and it is C4's entry.
- **No new op in the keep-map engine.** C1 is written with `or` and `eq`, which already exist. C3 adds **one field** to an existing transform and one conditional branch, and nothing else in `reader/expr.ts` moves.
- **No engine rule for any provider but claude and codex.** Nine other providers carry a `partWhen` and none is touched; nine other providers keep `"version": 1` and are not re-read.
- **No change to `dropCommands`.** The nine names stay, the drop still wins, and the 444 bare records that name one of them are still dropped. Adding or removing a name is a separate decision about what the person meant.
- **No copy decision.** `No messages yet` stays byte-for-byte, and C3's wording and C6's `0+` are the operator's rulings, recorded as his in the mechanism above and left to him.
- **No deletion of stored turns and no migration.** The map version bump replaces turns as a consequence of re-reading, inside the transaction `store.ts` already has. Nothing new deletes, nothing back-fills, and the overview schema does not move.
- **No change to harvest.** `cwd-newest` stays codex's key, `IDENTITY_HARVEST_KEYS` gains no member, `claimStrengthForKey` is not touched and no claim is re-rated. C2 is fixed in the reader, which is where the record's folder is already known; making a weak key strong is a manifest question and a different phase.
- **No change to `resolve.ts`'s fallback loops.** Both stay, because a session can `cd` and a project can be opened through a symlink. What is added is a comparison after the record is read, not a narrowing of where it is looked for.
- **Nothing acts on `'unknown'` as though it were `'different'`.** An absent or unreadable folder on either side leaves the row exactly as it reads today. That is the clause that stops this phase refusing a good record, and it is the one a later round is most likely to simplify away.
- **No status, no verb, no column and no channel.** Nothing here can set a session's status, end one, restore one or draw a row differently except in the two cells the counts already own.
- **No release.**


## Phase 300 — what a first read costs the person waiting (Phase 293's counts verifier, 2026-09-19)

**Subject.** `perf(overview): a first read stops holding the window`

**First body line.** `Phase 300: the counts read reads less, and the claude resolver stops re-scanning`

**Semver.** Patch. Nothing a person reads changes and no count moves. What changes is that the session manager's first pass over a store it has not read yet stops freezing the rest of the app while it reads: the window keeps painting, a keystroke in a terminal lands, and a session that was never prompted stops costing main a scan of every claude project directory on every ask. No cell's word, no column, no verb, no channel and no status moves, and Catch Me Up reads exactly what it reads today.

**Tier 3.** By CLAUDE.md's second question: `src/main/overview/reader/` is the ONE path every provider is read through, `src/main/overview/service.ts:288-296` is the one read call, and this phase changes what that path admits before it parses. A change there is a claim about every agent, so **the evidence is a per-row matrix over real data** and its first obligation is that no count moves for any provider. **The parent-commit measurement is mandatory whatever the tier** and doubly so here, because the operator's standing rule is that nothing gets worse and a performance phase can only prove that by measuring the same asks at the parent: a phase that makes a cold read fast and a warm ask slower has regressed, and the warm ask is the one a person makes all day. Three independent methods, one of them an attack: **measure the parent commit**, **attack rather than confirm** (drive the shapes in which this change is WORSE, listed in the proof), and **re-derive independently** (the main-thread gap read by two instruments that do not share a clock). It is not Tier 3 for the other reasons: the overview store is Tortie's own derived cache and never the source of truth for restore, the manifest is opened read only, nothing spawns, nothing holds a credential and nothing sends the person's words anywhere.

**Charter.** Phase 293's Tier 3 **counts verifier**, 2026-09-19. It returned findings C4 and C5 beside the three Phase 299 takes. Both are minor, both are inherited from the Phase 137 reader rather than caused by Phase 293, and both were **recorded as stated limits when 293 landed** at `f6c11f57`. `build/p293/SPEC.md:89-92` states them in §1's limits, in these words: "**One row's first read can hold main for as long as that record takes**: up to about 0.8 s for a 196 MB codex record, measured with the page cache warm. The refresh yields between rows, not inside one. Catch Me Up's own read yields nowhere, so this is no worse than today (C4). A claude row with no record yet costs a scan of `~/.claude/projects` on every ask, about 23 ms (C5)." `:2138-2139` states them again with the remedy each one wants — "one large record's first read holds main (C4: a worker, or slices); a claude row with no record scans `~/.claude/projects` on every ask (C5: cache the absent answer per id and folder)" — and `:2259` routes C5 to §9. The running log's landing line names both as "STILL NOT TRUE and each queued next as its own entry": "a first read of a large record can hold the main thread up to 797 ms, a claude row with no record stats every project directory". This is that entry for the two of them. Phase 299 takes C1 to C3; the Refresh that re-opens a closed remote project tab and the lost tombstone are separate entries and are not in this one.

**Which question each one is, plainly.** **C5 is a cache question.** The answer is recomputed on every ask and nothing about it has changed between asks. **C4 was queued as a scheduling question and the measurement below turns most of it into a reading question.** The counts channel needs four numbers and two clocks and it currently builds the path index to get them, and the path index is what forces 107 of a 187 MiB codex record through `JSON.parse`. What is left after the reading is fixed IS a scheduling question, it is stated as a remaining bound rather than closed, and it is not in this phase.

### What was measured before this entry was written, so no round re-derives it

The verifier's readings are quoted. Everything else was measured for this entry, read only, on **2026-09-19**, against the tree at origin/main's tip in `/private/tmp/wt-release` (which carries no `node_modules`, so every source reading is read and not executed) and against the real stores under the operator's home, which were statted and opened for reading and never written, moved or copied out.

**The verifier's numbers.** C4: up to **797 ms** for a **196 MB** codex record asked by Details on a Past row, **475 ms** for an idle Managed row, and a worst measured heartbeat gap of **322 ms**. C5: the inherited resolver stats all of `~/.claude/projects`, **2,775** directories, at a median of **23 ms** and a max of **59 ms** per row, and **575 of the 659 ms** of a warm pass over **161 rows**.

**The claude store, measured here.** `~/.claude/projects` holds **2,779 entries, 2,776 of them directories** — the three that are not are `.DS_Store`, `.cursorindexingignore` and `-Users-gdc-intent.zip`, and `resolve.ts:138-141` stats a `<id>.jsonl` path under every entry whatever it is. **The verifier's 2,775 and this 2,776 are the same directory counted at different moments through different doors**, his through the shipping resolver while the app was running and this one with `find` today, and a claude project directory is created the first time a session runs in a folder that has none, so the number drifts upward by ones — a re-measure that reads 2,777 is not a contradiction and the arithmetic below does not depend on the exact value. **21,156** `*.jsonl` records, **10.51 GB**; p50 **210,043** bytes, p90 **846,137**, p99 **5,828,968**, max **151,239,835** (144.2 MiB, and it is this session's own log).

**C5's cost, re-derived from the shipping arithmetic.** A script replicating `resolve.ts:134-142`'s claude arm for an id that has no record — the case that scans to the end and answers `no-file` — over the real directory, warm, twelve runs: **min 14.3 ms, median 19.5 ms, max 30.8 ms**. The `readdirSync` alone is **1.9 ms of that**, so **the listing is 10 percent of the cost and the 2,776 `statSync` calls are the other 90** — a cache of the LISTING buys almost nothing and a cache of the ANSWER buys nearly all of it. The verifier's 23 ms median is this number measured inside a main thread that is also doing other work, so the two agree.

**The codex store, measured here, and this is where C4 lives.** **26,312** `rollout-*.jsonl` records, **11.76 GB**. p50 **68,260** bytes, p90 **83,896**, p99 **5,954,144**, p99.9 **63,488,990**, mean **479,844**. **902** records are at or above 1 MiB, **367** above 4, **97** above 16, **51** above 32, **23** above 64, **15** above 100 and **7** at or above 196 MiB. **The largest is 1,006,098,515 bytes, 959.5 MiB**, five times the record the verifier measured, and it is not archival: it was last written on **2026-09-12**, and a 187 MiB record was written **today**.

**Where the 797 ms is not.** The byte scan is not the cost. `lines.ts:152-261`'s chunk loop, replicated with no parse, no fold and no keep map, over 1 MiB chunks as `lines.ts:159` uses: **53 ms for a 186.8 MiB record, 56 ms for a 190.6 MiB one and 233 ms for the 959.5 MiB one**, at 3.4 to 4.1 GiB/s warm. **Path extraction is not the cost either**, and this was a hypothesis worth killing so no builder chases it: only **0.9 MiB of text** reaches `reader/index.ts:119-141`'s `extractPathsFromText` for that 186.8 MiB record (4,535 blobs, 3,930 of them commands, 85,643 whitespace tokens), and the whitespace split `paths.ts:166` runs costs **3 ms**. **Nor is the store write**: that record holds **26** `task_complete` records, so `service.ts:322-332` inserts about twenty-six rows, and `store.ts:25-28` measures the store's whole growth at **0.166 percent** of log bytes.

**Where it is.** codex's prefilter, `keep-map.json:378-379`, reads a **200 byte** head, and its `item_completed` rule at **`:388-391`** is `class: "any"` with no second stage. On the **186.8 MiB** record the head admits **14,903 of 42,018 lines holding 109.3 MiB, 58.5 percent of the file**, of which the `item_completed` rule alone accounts for **13,946 lines and 107.4 MiB**; `JSON.parse` of the admitted lines is **151 ms**. So **that record's** measurable floor is **53 ms of scan plus 151 ms of parse, 204 ms**, the store write is twenty-six rows, and the remainder of the verifier's 797 ms is `reader/fold.ts` and `reader/expr.ts` over 13,946 parsed records and the garbage they make. Every part of that is pure JavaScript with no filesystem and no SQLite, and **that single fact is what the mechanism below turns on.** The 186.8 MiB record is not the verifier's 196 MB record, so the split is proportional and not exact, and measuring it exactly on one record is the phase's first step.

**Two narrowings measured and REJECTED, so no round re-derives them either.** A second-stage `requireAnywhere` on the `item_completed` rule naming `"AgentMessage"` or `"command"` — a field `lines.ts:86-90`'s `decideWhole` already applies — drops, on the 186.8 MiB record, **68 percent of the lines and only 10.5 percent of the bytes** (13,946 lines / 107.4 MiB down to 4,474 / 96.1 MiB) and costs **39 ms** to decide. The big lines are precisely the ones carrying `command`. And **claude has almost nothing to gain**: its paths rule is already a separate `class: "paths"` entry (`keep-map.json:289-296`) that `containers.ts:266` appends as `extra`, and dropping it on a real 112.2 MiB claude record moves the admitted bytes from **28.7 MiB to 24.0** and the parse from **27 ms to 17**. That 112.2 MiB claude record costs about **32 ms to decide and 27 ms to parse**. **C4 is a codex-shaped defect.**

**The one narrowing that pays, measured.** Dropping the path index for the counts read, so codex's `item_completed` lines survive only on `"AgentMessage"`: on the **186.8 MiB** record, **107.4 MiB and 13,946 lines become 0.5 MiB and 544 lines — 0.4 percent of the bytes — and the parse falls from 151 ms to 1 ms**, at a cost of **33 ms** of raw whole-line `indexOf` over the same bytes. On the **190.6 MiB** record it is **64.5 MiB and 263 `item_completed` lines down to 0.0 MiB and 39 lines**, decided in 15 ms and parsed in under 1. So the whole reduced read of the **186.8 MiB** record is about **53 ms of scan plus 33 ms of decide plus 1 ms of parse, 87 ms, against that same record's 204 ms today**, with the fold's share falling in proportion to the records it never sees.

**The source, read at origin/main's tip.**

- **C4's yield, exactly where it is.** `overview/activity.ts:29-33` says it: rows are brought up to date "one row at a time, yielding to the event loop between rows. The read is synchronous file work, and a hundred rows in one task would hold main still for as long as they take." The yield is `:138-143`, one `setImmediate`, and the loop is `:175-179` — `await yieldToEventLoop()` before every row but the first, then a synchronous `refreshRowForActivity`. `:36-40` and `:60-61` serialise whole calls on one module-level chain, so a second ask waits behind the first for the whole pass, not just the row.
- **The read the counts pay for.** `service.ts:435-449` calls `readOneRow` with `turnLimit` **0**, and `store.ts:687-694` turns that into `LIMIT 0`, so no turn is listed and no text crosses into JS. **Everything above the listing is paid in full**: the resolve, the whole-file scan, the parse, the fold, the path extraction and the insert of every turn and every path fact. `store.ts:130-159` and `:188-195` are why the counts themselves are cheap — `LIST_ACTIVITY_SQL` counts inside SQLite and carries no text.
- **It is a FIRST read, and Phase 299 is about to make every row pay one.** `service.ts:279-285` reuses a stored watermark only when `prior.mapVersionAtLastRead === mapVersion` and the path is unchanged, `containers.ts:277-286` answers `work: 'none'` on a bare stat match, and `watermark.ts:124-136` resumes from the offset for a file that only grew. So a running session's 30 s re-ask is a stat plus a tail, and 797 ms is the price of a record the store has not read at this map version. **Phase 299 bumps claude and codex to version 2**, which by its own account "pay their full read once at the next ask" — so the first sheet open after 299 lands pays C4 for every claude and codex row, and that is the run this phase must measure.
- **C5, and why it is paid warm as well as cold.** `service.ts:233-242` resolves BEFORE the watermark check at `:280`, so the scan is not something a warm store avoids. `resolve.ts:136-137` stats the direct path `<projects>/dashEncodeClaudeCwd(realCwd)/<id>.jsonl`; on a miss `:138-141` accepts `<id>.jsonl` under any entry of the projects directory. `resolve.ts:87-93`'s `listDir` is one `readdirSync` and `:79-85`'s `isFile` is one `statSync` per entry. A row that HAS a record at the direct path never enters the loop; a never-prompted row runs it to the end every time, and a row whose record sits elsewhere runs half of it on average. **`carryForward` (`service.ts:603-626`) stores `readState: 'no-file'` and nothing ever reads it to skip the next scan.**
- **Nothing else has this breadth.** The other fallback loops, counted today: `~/.cursor/chats` **52** entries, `~/.grok/sessions` **152**, `~/.gemini/tmp` **311** (and gemini's loop at `resolve.ts:265-273` does a `readFileSync` of `.project_root` per entry), `~/.pi/agent/sessions` **305**, `~/.omp/agent/sessions` **61**. claude is nine times the next largest. **The cache is claude's alone and a later round does not widen it without measuring.**
- **Where a mode flag can live with no schema change.** `store/schema.ts:33` is `OVERVIEW_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`, every statement is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, and **the file contains no `ALTER` and no migration step** — a bump adds a table and cannot add a column, and the only other path is the drop-and-recreate reserved for a store written by a newer build. But `schema.ts:51` declares `watermark TEXT -- JSON`, parsed at `store.ts:325` and written at `:623` and `:655`. **An optional field on the byte-offset watermark is a JSON value and not a column**, an old watermark with the field absent reads as "the paths were read", which is true of every row written before this phase, and the schema does not move.
- **The worker precedent, and its budget.** `src/main/symbols/worker.ts:11-15` records why that one was chosen: "PURE WASM… zero native code and zero codesigning burden." `pool.ts:4-21` records the budget as measured rather than guessed, six workers at the knee, never more than `cpus - 2`, "so indexing cannot starve the main thread and the tmux poll it runs", and it states the ceiling in one line: "A fourth home for search work means deleting one of them first." `proc/identity.ts:81-84` holds exactly **two** worker names. `containers.ts:14-20` and `resolve.ts:20` both import `better-sqlite3`, so the reader is not native-free.
- **The instrument already exists and needs no Electron.** `reader/index.ts:1-10` says the reader has "No Electron import and no React. The conformance probe runs this module under plain node", and `build/conformance-overview.mjs:61` and `:97-102` declare `--real <file> --provider <p> --repo <dir>`. That is what splits the 797 ms.
- **What a person feels and how often.** `renderer/session-manager/use-sheet-refresh.ts:12-22`: the counts are asked for every Managed id when the sheet opens, for a new id, for a changed id, **for every running id every 30 s while the sheet is visible**, and for a Past row when Details opens; status changes and the 30 s re-ask are joined into one call armed 1,500 ms later. `session-manager-slice.ts:287` sends **100 ids per call** against main's cap of 200 (`src/shared/overview.ts:276`), so the verifier's 161-row pass is two calls. `overview/ipc.ts:131-133` is an `invoke` handler, so for the length of one row's read main answers nothing at all: not this channel, not the window, not the tmux poll.

### The mechanism, as options with their costs

Five options. Each says what a person feels, what it costs to build and what could go wrong. The recommendation follows, and so does the one thing that is the operator's call.

1. **A worker or a utility process for the read.** *A person feels:* nothing ever stutters, whatever the record. This is the only option that makes the worst case invisible rather than smaller. *Cost:* high, and higher than it looks. CLAUDE.md's refusals allow Tortie's own code in a worker, and the pure-JavaScript half — scan, parse, fold, expression engine — moves cleanly, because the measurement above shows it touches no SQLite and its output is small enough to structure-clone (about twenty-six turns for a 187 MiB record, and 0.166 percent of log bytes overall). What does NOT move is `resolve.ts`, which opens `better-sqlite3` for muse, antigravity and cursor, and the store write, which opens it for everything. So a native-free worker leaves resolve and the insert on main, which means **it does not fix C5 at all** and it costs a third entry in `proc/identity.ts:81-84` against a budget `pool.ts:18-21` says has no free slot. *What could go wrong:* a second writer to `overview.db` if a later round moves the insert in too, which would put a durability question on a file that today is written in one transaction from one thread; a worker that outlives the ask on a laptop already running many agents, each thread holding a line buffer and, on a sorted-key vintage, a 4 MiB head; and a worker that dies mid-read, which today cannot happen because `service.ts:322-332` is one durable transaction on main.

2. **Slice a read so it yields inside one record.** *A person feels:* the worst gap falls to whatever the slice is, on every provider and every record, with no change to what is read. *Cost:* medium, and it lands on the shared engine. `lines.ts:141-144` already takes `{ start }` and `containers.ts:161-168` already creates one `Fold` per pass, so the state can be carried — but `scanFile` owns its loop and has no "stop after N bytes", so it becomes resumable or `jsonlPass` re-enters it and the `Fold` is handed in rather than created inside. *What could go wrong:* the watermark is only honest at a turn boundary and `watermark.ts:124-136` demands a newline before the offset plus two 4 KiB hashes, so a slice must never stamp one mid-turn; a record the agent appends to between two slices changes size and mtime, which is exactly the shape `checkByteOffset` turns into a full read, so a live session's big record could restart its read repeatedly and finish slower than today; and `activity.ts:60-61`'s queue holds the next ask for the whole sliced read, so per-row gaps fall while the wall time of a pass rises. That last one is a regression under the operator's rule and it is why this is not the first move.

3. **Cache the resolver's answer with an invalidation rule.** *A person feels:* a session that was never prompted stops costing 19 ms of main on every ask — the 575 of 659 ms the verifier measured in a warm pass over 161 rows. *Cost:* low. The cache is the **negative answer of the FALLBACK, keyed by id**, never the direct stat at `resolve.ts:136-137`, and it hangs off `ResolveEnv` (`resolve.ts:45-48`) so the function stays pure and a test hands it a fresh one.
